Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: New swelling of the left elbow noticed approximately 1 week ago.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset/duration: Noticed about one week prior while in the shower.
  - Symptoms: Visible swelling over the left elbow; described as slightly warm to touch and containing a bit of fluid sensation. Not painful at rest; can move elbow normally. Tip of elbow not painful on direct pressure; area adjacent to the swelling feels "weird" and slightly uncomfortable.
  - Progression: Patient reports it feels a bit better now but no clear improvement course documented.
- Past medical history:
  - Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
  - Otherwise reports being fit and well.
- Medications:
  - None regularly.
- Social history:
  - Occupation: Desk-based job (not physically demanding).
  - Exercise: Runs 2–3 times per week.
- Allergies:
  - Peanuts. No documented drug allergies.

Objective:
- Exam findings (left elbow):
  - Visible swelling over the left elbow.
  - Area slightly warmer compared with adjacent skin.
  - Tip of the elbow: skin noted as dry; not tender on direct pressure at the tip.
  - Adjacent to the swelling: patient reports a peculiar sensation and some discomfort with pressure.
  - Range of motion: patient able to move elbow normally; no limitation of movement documented.
- Clinician impression during exam:
  - Exam not suggestive of septic arthritis at this time.
- Investigations:
  - None performed during the visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling (olecranon bursitis):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Olecranon bursitis.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Septic bursitis/infected bursa.
     - Gout involving the olecranon bursa.
     - Inflammatory/rheumatologic arthritis involving periarticular structures.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Blood tests (forms to be mailed): inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibody panel, and tests to evaluate for gout (full screen as described).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Start ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
     - Advise to seek urgent review (phone/video or in-person) if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, or redness spreads.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - None documented.

2. Osteoarthritis (past diagnosis):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Osteoarthritis (history; previously diagnosed by GP).
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable for this visit.
   - Investigations planned:
     - None specific to osteoarthritis documented for this visit.
   - Treatment planned:
     - No change to management documented.

Follow-up:
- Blood test forms to be mailed to the patient with instructions for where to have tests drawn.
- Results expected in approximately 5–6 days after testing; arrange follow-up appointment (phone, video, or face-to-face per patient preference) to review results and re-examine the elbow.
- Patient instructed to contact clinic sooner if symptoms worsen or signs of infection develop.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs were not documented.
  - No detailed medication reconciliation beyond patient statement of no regular meds.
  - No documentation of exact nature/type of peanut allergy (reaction type/severity).
  - No procedure (e.g., aspiration) performed or discussed beyond blood tests.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Transcript generally clear with minimal inaudible segments; some conversational fillers removed in documentation.
